subject.title: Feature: Pre-compaction agent notification, structured handoff window, and deferral mechanism

question: Should OpenClaw add first-class pre-threshold compaction warnings, a structured handoff/checkpoint turn, and bounded agent-requested compaction deferral to core, or keep current memoryFlush/notifyUser/hook/checkpoint behavior as the supported lifecycle?
rationale: The request changes compaction timing, persisted session semantics, public config, and authority handling across compaction boundaries, so automation cannot choose the product and security contract safely.

options.title: Design Core Lifecycle
options.body: Define warning thresholds, handoff checkpoint schema, deferral authorization rules, and upgrade behavior before implementation.

options.title: Narrow To Notices
options.body: Limit core work to earlier visible warning improvements and leave handoff deferral authority out of scope for now.

options.title: Keep Existing Model
options.body: Treat memoryFlush, notifyUser, compaction hooks, and checkpoint metadata as the supported lifecycle and decline new core deferral surface.

recommendation.title: Design Core Lifecycle
recommendation.body: Define warning thresholds, handoff checkpoint schema, deferral authorization rules, and upgrade behavior before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest available routing candidate for the current compaction lifecycle and security/product boundary decision.
